LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.5: Interactive Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Interactive Speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How else do you communicate without use of speech?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
2. use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
3. use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication
4. use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations
5. show enthusiasm to engage in conversations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Interactive Speaking helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions

What this means
In this part you learn to use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Interactive Speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Show enthusiasm to engage in conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to show enthusiasm to engage in conversations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show enthusiasm to engage in conversations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Interactive Speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show enthusiasm to engage in conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Interactive Speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Interactive Speaking to a partner. (skill: use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Interactive Speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement.
3. Practise this skill: use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions.
4. Practise this skill: use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Interactive Speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Interactive Speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Interactive Speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How else do you communicate without use of speech?
2. Why is attention important when listening?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Interactive Speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement.
5. Be able to: use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
